headline_marked: 33 BGB platoons [[deployed across industrial hubs]] to ensure stability
headline: 33 BGB platoons deployed across industrial hubs to ensure stability
summary: Border Guard Bangladesh troops are stationed in Dhaka, Gazipur, and Narayanganj following garment worker unrest over minimum wage demands.
details: Thirty-three platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) have been deployed across key industrial corridors in Dhaka, Gazipur, and Narayanganj to maintain order following unrest in the readymade garments sector.
The deployment covers critical areas including Savar, Ashulia, and Mirpur in Dhaka; several hubs in Narayanganj; and multiple locations in Gazipur, including Chandra and Kashimpur.
BGB headquarters is monitoring field operations in real-time via a tech-supported surveillance room with video feeds to ensure rapid response and security.
The paramilitary force is operating alongside local administration and police to protect lives, property, and supply chains while ensuring factories continue to operate normally.
The unrest was triggered by garment workers demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000, with some protests turning violent and involving clashes with police.
Tensions have since eased after the minimum wage board held its first meeting on November 4, announcing that a revised wage structure will take effect in December.
Workers are expected to see the revised wages reflected in their pay packets starting in January, ending the current five-year wage cycle.
For context, the last minimum wage revision in November 2023 saw the minimum wage increase from Tk 8,000 to Tk 12,500, a 56.25 percent rise.
caption:
33 BGB platoons are on high alert across Dhaka, Gazipur, and Narayanganj. Why the sudden surge in security?

Thirty-three platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) have been deployed across key industrial corridors in Dhaka, Gazipur, and Narayanganj to maintain order following unrest in the readymade garments sector.

The deployment covers critical areas including Savar, Ashulia, and Mirpur in Dhaka; several hubs in Narayanganj; and multiple locations in Gazipur, including Chandra and Kashimpur.

BGB headquarters is monitoring field operations in real-time via a tech-supported surveillance room with video feeds to ensure rapid response and security.

The paramilitary force is operating alongside local administration and police to protect lives, property, and supply chains while ensuring factories continue to operate normally.

The unrest was triggered by garment workers demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000, with some protests turning violent and involving clashes with police.

Tensions have since eased after the minimum wage board held its first meeting on November 4, announcing that a revised wage structure will take effect in December.

Workers are expected to see the revised wages reflected in their pay packets starting in January, ending the current five-year wage cycle.

For context, the last minimum wage revision in November 2023 saw the minimum wage increase from Tk 8,000 to Tk 12,500, a 56.25 percent rise.
